Subject: Dedicated capacity ask for Q1 launch - US/EU/APAC

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week — LaunchAI is moving faster than expected and we need to lock in a predictable dedicated runway ahead of our Q1 public launch window. Attached is our initial traffic forecast and token profile (launchai_traffic_forecast_q4.xlsx). High level: 600 qps peak across inference (prompt+streaming), 60/25/15 traffic split US/EU/APAC, average sequence length ~850 tokens, and a ~10% heavy-context cohort that requires sustained KV caching.

Can Redwood provide a recommended tri-region dedicated footprint (GPU counts by region, suggested failover lanes, and a short SOW for a two-tranche commitment)? We also need rough per-token unit economics to model into our procurement ask.

Timeline: we need a draft SOW and runway numbers by Oct 28 to feed into our procurement cycle.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Nair
Head of Platform Partnerships, LaunchAI
priya@launchai.ai

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-23T13:26:00-07:00
Subject: LaunchAI capacity sketch (v1) for Rafael

Team — I pulled the spreadsheet and sketched a conservative runway. Summary (see attached capacity_sketch_v1.pdf):

- Baseline traffic assumption: 600 qps peak, token mix and seq length as provided.
- Recommended steady-state dedicated:
  - US: 48 x A100-equivalent GPUs (sustained target for 60% of traffic),
  - EU: 20 x A100-equivalent GPUs (25% traffic),
  - APAC: 12 x A100-equivalent GPUs (15% traffic).

- Canary/burst backstop: reserve a 20% burst pool in each region (hot spare nodes) and a cross-region failover lane (US -> EU, EU -> APAC) with auto-routing for degraded local capacity.
- KV caching: allocate 25% of GPU memory budget to hot-KV cache for the 10% heavy-context cohort; expected to reduce steady per-token latency by ~12% and effective cost by ~8%.
- Cost levers: quantization to int8 yields ~1.6x throughput on eligible models; recommend phased quantization for quality-sensitive endpoints.
- Operational asks from sales: confirmed SLO (p95 latency target), data residency constraints for EU, and preferred contract term (12 vs 24 months) to finalize tranche mix.

Attachments: capacity_sketch_v1.pdf (PDF, 210 KB)

I left margin notes where we make conservative assumptions (e.g., traffic autocorrelation and peak concurrency). If Rafael wants, I can convert numbers into a tranche-based SOW pricing table for Oct 28.

— Irene
Irene Choi, Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Nair <priya@launchai.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, contracts@launchai.ai
Date: 2026-10-26T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: LaunchAI proposed runway + next steps (SOW link)

Priya — attached is our proposed runway and a short mutual action plan. Key points from the internal sizing (see also Irene's sketch):

- Proposed committed nodes (baseline tranche 1, 12-month): US 40 GPUs, EU 18 GPUs, APAC 10 GPUs.
- Canary/burst approach: 20% regional burst capacity + cross-region failover lane.
- Expected blended unit cost (post-caching and batching): $0.0019 per token (estimate; final pricing in SOW).
- Rollout: Tranche 1 active at contract start; Tranche 2 (additional 25% capacity) deployable within 60 days upon traffic trigger.

Action items:
1) Review and confirm region residency constraints and preferred term (12 vs 24 months).
2) Sign SOW: SOW_LaunchAI_v1.docx (attached) — we can send via DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/Sign?documentId=LAUNCHAI-SOW-1
3) Kickoff ops sync the week of Nov 2 for canary choreography and routing policies.

Forwarding Irene's notes inline below for transparency.

Attachments: SOW_LaunchAI_v1.docx (DOCX, 42 KB)

Rafael Mendes
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
